issues.display_title: Issue #105: Invite unregistered emails: project_invitations table + claim on register
issues.main_description_html:
RESULT 24/07/26

✅ Implementation: Invite Unregistered Emails (Task #105 / PR #113 )

Overview

members/Create used to return 404 "no user with that email" when a project
owner invited someone who had not signed up yet — a dead end. This task replaces
that 404 with a persistent invitation that is claimed automatically the moment
the invited email creates an account (email or Google), joining them to the
project with the role they were invited at.

Code Implementation

  1. project_invitations table (src/models/models.go):

    • New ProjectInvitation model (id, project_id, email lowercase, role,
      invited_by, claimed_at nullable, timestamps) with a unique index on
      (project_id, email). Mirrors the ProjectMember pattern: manual
      ID/timestamps, BeforeCreate UUID hook, no soft-delete.
    • Registered in AllModels() so GORM AutoMigrate provisions it, and backed by
      an explicit SQL migration (migrations/202607240001_add_project_invitations.sql)
      using CREATE TABLE / UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS so both paths coexist
      idempotently.

  2. Invitation branch (src/action/v1/members/create.go):

    • On gorm.ErrRecordNotFound for the target email, upsert a ProjectInvitation
      (FirstOrCreate(...).Assign(Role)) keyed on (project_id, email) — so a
      re-invite updates the pending role instead of erroring — and respond
      201 {"invited": true, "email": ...}. The existing-user path (add member +
      collaborator email) is unchanged.

  3. Claim helper (src/action/v1/members/claim.go):

    • ClaimInvitations(db, userID, email) loads every unclaimed invitation for
      the email, upserts a ProjectMember with the invited role (idempotent for a
      user who is already a member), and stamps claimed_at. It accepts a
      *gorm.DB so callers run it inside their own transaction or standalone.

  4. Claim wiring — proven ownership only (src/action/v1/auth/verifyEmail.go,
    src/action/v1/auth/google.go):

    • Email registration produces an unverified account, so claiming happens
      inside the VerifyEmail transaction — after email ownership is proven —
      rather than at register time (which would let anyone claim a victim's
      invitations by registering their email first).
    • Google verifies the email upstream, so the Google flow claims immediately on
      auto-provision, and also when it lifts a previously-unverified existing
      account to verified (see Task #113 review fix).

Testing

  • members/claim_test.go: claim creates member with invited role + stamps
    claimed_at; idempotent re-claim and already-member role upsert.
  • routes/v1/role_matrix_test.go: invite-unknown returns 201 {invited:true} and
    writes a single invitation row; re-invite upserts the role.

Sprint #100 / PRD gothru-3d-floormap#349 ("Unregistered email → offer to send a join-MapThru invitation").

Description

members/Create currently returns 404 "no user with that email" for unknown emails. Replace with an invitation flow:

  • Migration: project_invitations (id, project_id, email lowercase, role, invited_by, created_at, claimed_at nullable), unique (project_id, email). No expiry column — PRD open question 2 stays open; add later if product decides.
  • members/create.go: on ErrRecordNotFound for the target user → upsert invitation, respond 201 {"invited": true, "email": ...} (re-invite updates role)
  • Claim on account creation: after user create in both auth/register.go and auth/google.go, look up invitations by email → insert project_members rows with the invited role, stamp claimed_at

Why

Sprint item "Implement invite join mapthru email"; today inviting a colleague who hasn't signed up is a dead end.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Inviting an unknown email creates an invitation row (no more 404)
  • Response distinguishes added member vs invitation — FE notified: contract change
  • Registering (email or Google) with an invited email auto-joins the projects with the invited role
  • Re-invite updates the pending invitation's role
  • Tests: invite-unknown, claim-on-register, claim-on-google, re-invite
  • Build + tests green

Dependencies

None (email send is the follow-up task).

RESULT 24/07/26

✅ Implementation: Send Join-MapThru Invitation Email (Task #106 / PR #113 )

Overview

Follow-up to Task #105. When an invitation is created for an email that has no
account yet, MapThru now sends a "join MapThru" email inviting that person to
create an account so they can accept the invitation. Delivery is fire-and-forget
so a bounced email can never fail the invitation that already landed in the
database.

Code Implementation

  1. Plunk template ID (src/config/templates.go):

    • New TemplateJoinInvite constant holding the Plunk template ID
      (5f3257e0-8dae-4600-b607-cfae0b6251ad). The email design and copy live in
      the Plunk dashboard; the backend only triggers the template with data. The
      markup used to build that template is checked in at
      docs/email-templates/join-invite.html.

  2. Email service method (src/services/email.go):

    • SendJoinInviteEmail(toEmail, inviterName, projectName, registerLink) fires
      the TemplateJoinInvite event with inviter, project_name, url, and
      email data fields. The recipient has no account yet, so there is no
      fullname field (unlike the collaborator-added email).

  3. Fire-and-forget trigger (src/action/v1/members/create.go):

    • In the invitation branch (Task #105), after the invitation is upserted, the
      handler loads the project name and calls
      go emailService.SendJoinInviteEmail(email, user.Name, project.Name, link)
      where link = FRONTEND_URL/register. The same policy as the existing
      collaborator-added email: the goroutine's error is intentionally ignored so
      a Plunk failure never fails the stored invitation.

Testing

  • services/email_test.go (TestSendJoinInviteEmail): asserts the correct
    template ID, recipient, and every data field (inviter, project_name, url,
    email) reach Plunk, using the shared capture-server harness.

Sprint #100 / PRD gothru-3d-floormap#349.

Description

When an invitation is created for an unregistered email (#105), send the "join MapThru" email:

  • Template in Plunk dashboard ("X invited you to project Y on MapThru — create your account" + register link) — needs Plunk dashboard access
  • Const TemplateJoinInvite in src/config/templates.go
  • SendJoinInviteEmail(toEmail, inviterName, projectName, registerLink) on EmailService
  • Fire-and-forget from the invitation branch in members/create.go

Acceptance Criteria

  • Inviting an unregistered email sends the join email
  • Email failure does not fail the invitation (async)
  • Build + tests green

Dependencies

Blocked by #105 (invitation flow). Plunk dashboard access for template creation.
